summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which found no Manipur-specific trans law, enforcement series or incident pattern, and records it among the states/UTs that have not constituted the legally mandated transgender welfare board; the 2026 amendment narrowing legal recognition applies to it nationally. No deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); it is therefore assessed at the national score.

sources.summary: Human Rights Watch statement (26 March 2026) on India's 2026 Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, passed by parliament: removes self-identification, limits legal recognition to historically accepted socio-cultural groups such as hijra and kinner plus intersex people, mandates medical certification for recognition, and adds offences carrying up to life imprisonment for "coercing or alluring" someone to be transgender; only about 32,500 of the census-recorded 487,803 transgender persons hold ID cards. A national law applying uniformly to Manipur; no Manipur-specific deviation is reported.

BBC report (26 March 2026): both houses passed the amendment to the 2019 Act removing the right to self-identify, restricting recognition to biological/physical traits, intersex variations and traditional community identities, and requiring medical-board certification for gender-affirming surgery; protests from the community and opposition, a Supreme Court-appointed advisory panel asked for withdrawal, and presidential assent is pending. Applies nationally including Manipur, with no region-specific coverage in the piece.

Times of India (Kolkata edition, 18 August 2024): a transwoman alleged a Railway Protection Force constable groped her for a "gender check" at Rabindra Sadan metro station while she travelled to an RG Kar Medical College protest; RPF and Metro Railway denied the allegation and filed a counter-FIR. A West Bengal incident, not about Manipur, carried here as a national datapoint on security screening conduct toward gender-nonconforming people in public spaces.
